previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with a two-week history of abdominal distention, nausea, poor appetite, and constipation, with a single episode of vomiting on the day of admission. She has a complex medical history including chronic graft-versus-host disease, gastroparesis, and chronic opiate use for back pain. Abdominal X-ray revealed fecal loading, supporting constipation as a primary contributor to her symptoms. She was treated with an enema and bowel prep, which resolved her nausea and improved her abdominal discomfort. She underwent an EGD and colonoscopy, which revealed gastric nodules and a colonic ulcer with inflammation; biopsies were taken to evaluate for medication effects, infection, or GVHD. Dicyclomine was discontinued, metoclopramide was increased, and she was discharged on daily Miralax to prevent recurrence. She tolerated oral intake, remained stable, and was discharged home in improved condition with plans to follow up on biopsy results and with her GI specialist.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with h/o CML w/ myeloblastic crisis s/p Myeloablative 
stem cell transplant in ___ c/b GVHD on chronic prednisone and 
monthly IVIG infusions, with chronic n/v/abd pain attributed to 
bacterial overgrowth and gastroparesis, with recent 
hospitalization ___ for n/v/d, returns with recurrent symptoms 
of n/v/diarrhea workup revealed Rotavirus Ag and MRE imaging 
showing sigmoid colitis all consistent with Rotavirus colitis.
   
# Acute refractory Rotavirus Gastroenteritis:
# Acute on chronic abdominal pain
# Nausea with Vomiting 
# Hx bacterial overgrowth and gastroparesis
Sx of abdominal pain with n/v/d most consistent with 
gastroenteritis especially given immunosuppressed state, and 
slow to resolve process.  Recent normal CT scan.  GI was 
consulted and agreed with this assessment.  Colonic biopsy from 
last hospitalization returned with colitis, ulceration, and 
apoptosis.  GVHD was felt unlikely, as well as IBD. MRE with 
mucosal hyper enhancement also consistent with colitis. Work up 
revealed +rotavirus antigen. Given the positive Rotavirus Ag, 
MRE result, C-Scope biopsies and symptoms her presentation most 
consistent with viral gastroenteritis on top of her chronic 
abdominal symptoms. She was treated with aggressive supportive 
care, diet advanced slowly, IVFs, IV pain meds and antiemetics. 
Prior to discharge she was tolerating a regular diet and 
maintaining adequate hydration. Pain and nausea also well 
controlled. Given ODT Ondansetron to take at home until symptoms 
resolved. Her home laxatives and stool softeners held in house, 
she was instructed not to restart at home until her symptoms 
abate. 
  
# UTI 
Acute complicated bacterial UTI given immunosuppression. Urine 
culture returned with +Enterococcus, sensitive to nitrofurantoin 
(note she has had 2 positive cultures in the last 10 days. On 
Chronic bactrim for prophylaxis). Treated with Nitrofurantoin 
for plan ___ course fom ___.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  MR ___

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with CML s/p SCT with GVHD, CVID on IVIG,
presents with ongoing abd pain, diarrhea, and colonic bx with colitis unclear
etiology // evaluate small intestine for presence of inflammation or infection

TECHNIQUE:  T1 and T2-weighted multiplanar images of the abdomen and pelvis
were acquired within a 1.5 T magnet, including 3D dynamic sequences performed
prior to, during, and following the administration of 0.1 mmol/kg of Gadavist
intravenous contrast (7 cc). Oral contrast consisted of 900 mL of VoLumen. 1.0
mg of Glucagon was administered IM to reduce bowel peristalsis.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior imaging, the last are CT from ___ and MRCP
from ___.

FINDINGS: 

MR ENTEROGRAPHY:

The caliber and appearance of the small bowel is normal.  There are no
abnormally dilated or strictured segments.  The small bowel wall has normal
thickness and enhancement.  Bowel motility is normal.
Diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon is present.  Mild mucosal hyper
enhancement in the nondistended sigmoid colon (1101:57) suggests colitis, but
is nonspecific and may be secondary to underdistention.

MRI OF THE ABDOMEN WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:

Visualized portions of the liver have homogeneous signal and enhancement. 
There is no intra or extra-hepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is
surgically absent.
There is atrophy of the pancreatic parenchyma.  The main pancreatic duct is
normal in caliber.  Pancreatic cystic lesions are seen throughout the
pancreas, the largest in the head measures 2.1 x 1.3 cm (05:18).
The kidneys and adrenals are normal.  Subcentimeter cortical renal cyst is
seen in the upper pole of the right kidney (14:28).  There is a single renal
artery present bilaterally.
The spleen is normal in size and signal.

MRI OF THE PELVIS WITH AND WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:

The bladder is normal.  The uterus and adnexa are normal.
There is no free fluid in the abdomen and pelvis.
There is no retroperitoneal, mesenteric or pelvic lymphadenopathy.
There is patchy hyper enhancement of the bone marrow in the sacrum
bilaterally, crossing the midline (13:64), in atypical appearance for a stress
fracture.  These area is not included in the imaging on T1 or STIR.  Dedicated
pelvic MRI is recommended to exclude infiltrative process.

IMPRESSION: 

1.  No evidence of inflammation throughout the small bowel.  Mild mucosal
hyper enhancement in the nondistended sigmoid colon suggests colitis, but is
nonspecific and may be secondary to underdistention.
2.  Patchy enhancement within the sacrum bilaterally, not fully characterized.

RECOMMENDATION(S):  Dedicated pelvic MRI is recommended to exclude
infiltrative process.

signaling in pelvis, history of acute on chronic headaches, please eval for

There is slight osteopenia throughout the calvarium ; however, no focal lytic
